title: Main Gate
subtitle: Territory, context and historical journey
summary: Welcome to the complex and an introduction to its setting, followed by the main historical transformations of La Cartuja.
locationText: Main gate of the Monastery. Coordinate supplied by the INNOPAT team.
mainContent: Introduction to the surrounding landscape: façade, Aljarafe, Guadalquivir, Triana and Isla de la Cartuja.
Working historical overview: Guadalquivir clays, Almohad precedents, Carthusian foundation, Napoleonic invasion, confiscation, the Pickman period, Expo ’92 and current uses.
science: Geoarchaeology: Guadalquivir sedimentary deposits and clays and their relationship with pottery production.
anecdote: Tradition concerning the origin of the pottery “caves” and the discovery of the Virgin. Documentary review pending.
extra: 3D model of the Almohad kiln preserved beneath the IAPH.

title: Outer Chapel and Gatehouse
subtitle: The threshold of silence and Carthusian life
summary: The boundary between the outside world and enclosure explains isolation, devotion and the organisation of Carthusian life.
locationText: Outer Chapel and Gatehouse. Coordinate supplied by the INNOPAT team.
mainContent: The Outer Chapel as a threshold between the outside world and enclosure.
Carthusian life: cells, gardens, prayer, communal meals and walks.
The porter as the monastery’s practical link with the outside.
science: Architecture of isolation: entrances, routes and spatial separation serving the Carthusian rule.
anecdote: Women’s access and enclosure boundaries: planned content pending documentary verification.
extra: Interactive diagram of enclosed and public areas.
Additional information about the Meat Kitchen.

title: From the Entrance Atrium to the Church Portal
subtitle: Life inside the walls
summary: Production, service and management spaces that explain the monastery’s everyday operation.
locationText: From the entrance atrium to the church portal. Coordinate supplied by the INNOPAT team.
mainContent: Stables, guest accommodation and food assistance.
Enclosed monks and lay brothers: different roles within the community.
Meat Kitchen, Prior’s House, monastic prison and transition towards the inner courtyards.
science: Monastic self-sufficiency: management of water, livestock, supplies and resources.
anecdote: Carthusian horses and the monastic prison as possible interpretive stories. Validation pending.
extra: Additional content on Carthusian livestock breeding.

title: The Church Portal and Adjacent Chapels
subtitle: Archaeological recovery, Columbus and the Baroque
summary: Archaeology, restoration and historical memory at the church portal and its adjacent chapels.
locationText: Church portal and adjacent chapels. Coordinate supplied by the INNOPAT team.
mainContent: Archaeological recovery and restoration after industrial transformations.
Cladding, rose window, paintings, and the chapels of Saint Bruno and Saint Catherine.
Library, Columbian tradition and residential changes during the Pickman period.
science: Innovation in ceramic cladding and the evolution of tile-making techniques.
anecdote: Noble memory, royal visits and symbolic conflicts: planned topics requiring documentary verification.
extra: Technical interview about the archaeological intervention.
Video on the evolution of the ceramic production space.
Possible alternative route depending on access to CAAC.

title: Inside the Church and the Chapel of Saint Anne
subtitle: From church to pottery drying room
summary: The transformation of a liturgical space into part of the Pickman industrial complex.
locationText: Inside the church and Chapel of Saint Anne. Coordinate supplied by the INNOPAT team.
mainContent: Liturgical use and the later dispersal of part of the movable heritage.
Industrial reuse of the nave for drying and storage.
Vaults, plasterwork and ceramic remains in the Chapel of Saint Anne.
science: Industrial archaeology: ventilation and spatial adaptation for ceramic drying processes.
anecdote: Columbus’s burial is one of the proposed stories for this stop; chronology and wording require review.
extra: Historical photo gallery of the church during the factory period.

title: Sacristy, Small Cloister and Adjacent Rooms
subtitle: The noble core and funerary memory
summary: The sacristy, small cloister, refectory, chapels and chapter house bring together art, funerary memory and different historical periods.
locationText: Sacristy, small cloister and adjacent rooms. Coordinate supplied by the INNOPAT team.
mainContent: Sacristy: liturgical elements, circulation, plasterwork and tiles.
Small cloister and Ribera Chapel as the noble and funerary core.
Refectory, Chapel of Saint Mary Magdalene and Chapter House.
science: Continuity and technological change in ceramics, from early modern production to nineteenth-century industrialisation.
anecdote: The archaeological search for the supposed early hermitage forms part of the planned story and must be documented precisely.
extra: Interpretive signage and reading of funerary elements.

title: The Great Cloister
subtitle: The monks’ cells and the industrial imprint
summary: The great cloister explains the individual life of the Carthusians and its later transformation during the factory period.
locationText: Great cloister and former cell area. Coordinate supplied by the INNOPAT team.
mainContent: Monks’ cells arranged around the great cloister.
Galleries and walkways as keys to reconstructing the original circulation.
Industrial transformation and Cell P as a teaching example.
science: Thermal engineering and the use of heat during the industrial period. Specific technical validation pending.
anecdote: Cell numbering and structural transformations as traces of the space’s successive uses.
extra: Visual reconstruction of a Carthusian cell with room, staircase, gallery and garden.

title: The Prior’s House
subtitle: The independent residence
summary: The prior’s residence explains government, representation and functional differentiation within the monastery.
locationText: Prior’s House and associated cloister. Coordinate supplied by the INNOPAT team.
mainContent: The distinct residential organisation of the Prior’s House.
Government and representative functions.
Relationship between this space and the exit route.
science: Spatial organisation: separation of administration, representation and eremitic enclosure.
anecdote: The prior as intermediary and manager of property and external relations.
extra: Reflection on possible future cultural uses of rooms and courtyards.

title: The Gardens
subtitle: The agricultural and productive space
summary: The gardens reveal the monastery’s agricultural dimension and the transformations of the industrial period.
locationText: Historic gardens and orchards. Coordinate supplied by the INNOPAT team.
mainContent: The monastic agricultural space and its later transformation.
Waterwheels, hydraulic structures and other production elements.
Architectural and archaeological remains integrated into the gardens.
science: Archaeology and in-situ display of remains recovered during interventions.
anecdote: The Galapaguera is a distinctive element planned for the story; its exact function must be reviewed.
extra: Visual tour of irrigation systems, waterwheels and freestanding industrial architecture.

title: The Ombú
subtitle: A botanical and historical tree
summary: A remarkable tree connects landscape, Atlantic exchanges and Columbian memory.
locationText: Ombú in the monastery gardens. Coordinate supplied by the INNOPAT team.
mainContent: Presentation of Phytolacca dioica as a distinctive landscape element.
Interpretive relationship with botanical exchanges and American memory.
science: Botany and history: circulation and acclimatisation in Seville of species originating in the Americas.
anecdote: Its planting by Hernando Colón must be presented as tradition unless a source confirms it.
extra: Botanical resource about the species, conservation and possible dating studies.

title: Lay Brothers’ Cloister
subtitle: The operational heart and present home of the IAPH
summary: The route ends in a space associated with the lay brothers and now integrated into the IAPH headquarters.
locationText: Lay Brothers’ Cloister, IAPH headquarters. Coordinate supplied by the INNOPAT team.
mainContent: A space connecting rooms associated with the lay brothers.
Architectural parallels that help explain how the cloister worked.
Current use as part of the headquarters of the Andalusian Institute of Historical Heritage.
science: The material received for Science / Archaeology of Production is incomplete and remains to be finished.
extra: Pending completion: the source summary ends incompletely at this stop.
transcript: Working content pending completion and validation.
